title: Trained recurrent model preserves cue geometry across a memory delay
summary: A trained256-unit recurrent model of context-dependent decisions retained cue-specific population geometry across a delay despite changing single-unit activity. Numerical subspace analysis linked low-activity delay states with later context-specific integration. This is a conditional computational interpretation, not a newly observed biological memory mechanism.

source_review.scope: Actual relevant primary computational/clinical Methods, model/result context and limitations read; no operational biological protocols

evidence.ai_role: Training the recurrent weights for a delayed contextual task creates the dynamics being analyzed; epoch-specific subspace analysis tests how learned cue representations persist and guide integration.
evidence.tested: Original model/training Methods and cue-delay/manifold Results were read. The model learned color-versus-motion context rules, and numerical trajectories and fixed/slow points were analyzed within its fitted dynamics.
evidence.unknown: Known mixed-selectivity, dynamic-memory and low-activity theories are substantial precedents, limiting novelty. The analysis concerns a trained artificial model, without new neural recordings or independent biological validation. Dale-type excitatory/inhibitory constraints and biological plasticity were not implemented; numerical line-attractor analysis is not a formal proof or a universal account of working memory.
